title: Separability after adjoining roots of the coefficients of a minimal polynomial
statement: Let K→K'→Ω and K→Ω be a commuting tower of fields [def-pc-field-extension]. Let p be an exponential characteristic of K', let e be a natural number, and let x∈Ω. Suppose x^(p^e) is separable over K [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and each nonzero coefficient c of its minimal polynomial over K has a p^e-th root in K'. Then x is separable over K'.

source.place: Fields, Tag 031V, coefficientwise Frobenius argument; the direct minimal-polynomial variant proved as IsSeparable.of_pow_of_coeffs in the source library

proof.text: Let q=p^e and let g be the minimal polynomial over K of x^q, mapped to K'. Lift its finitely many nonzero coefficients through the q-th-power map, and lift zero by zero, obtaining h in K'[T] with coefficientwise iterated Frobenius equal to g.

The polynomial g is separable because the minimal polynomial of x^q is separable and coprimality with its derivative is preserved by coefficient extension. Injectivity of iterated Frobenius on K' and the separable-map equivalence show h is separable.

Evaluating coefficientwise Frobenius and substituting T^q gives h(x)^q=g(x^q)=0. Exponential characteristic is positive, so q>0 and the field Ω has no nonzero nilpotents; hence h(x)=0. The minimal polynomial of x over K' divides h, and a divisor of a separable polynomial is separable. This is exactly the proved source declaration IsSeparable.of_pow_of_coeffs.
